subject: Budget Transparency Ordinance
overview: The Council approved a landmark Budget Ordinance on first reading to mandate fiscal transparency and initiated the first update to Medford's linkage fee structure since 1990. The body also granted a special permit for a new clinic at 1 Cabot Road and discussed critical staffing and morale issues within the Fire Department.

items.title: Meeting Records and Committee Reports
items.summary: Approved the March 12 meeting records and accepted committee reports regarding zoning reform, a new council newsletter strategy, and wildlife feeding regulations.

items.title: Special Permit for 1 Cabot Road
items.summary: Approved a special permit with conditions for Cambridge Health Alliance to establish an outpatient medical facility, including primary care and orthopedics, at 1 Cabot Road.

items.title: Fire Department Personnel Well-Being
items.summary: Discussed staffing shortages and morale with Fire Union President Buckley, approving a plan to organize station tours for elected officials to inspect deteriorating facility conditions.

items.title: Fire Chief Civil Service Process
items.summary: Placed on file a resolution calling for a meeting on the Fire Chief appointment process after receiving notice that the administration requested a two-month delay.

items.title: Budget Ordinance First Reading
items.summary: Approved a new Budget Ordinance on first reading to establish a transparent fiscal timeline and mandate quarterly financial reports to the Council.

items.title: Linkage Fee Update Request
items.summary: Formally requested that city planning staff update development linkage fee formulas, which have not been adjusted for inflation since their establishment in 1990.

items.title: Linkage Fee Ordinance Reforms
items.summary: Referred resolutions to align linkage fee administrative authority with state law and create a dedicated funding 'bucket' for affordable housing to the Administration and Finance Committee.

items.title: School Budget Shortfall Update
items.summary: Received an update regarding the school department's fiscal 2024 budget, noting that a previously projected $2.5 million shortfall was reduced to $216,000 after accounting corrections.
